experiment.name: vocab-context-input
experiment.hypothesis: 원래 단어가 남은 지문 때문에 원문과 다름을 문맥 모순으로 오인한다. 검사에 바뀐 단어가 반영된 전체 지문을 주는 입력 하나만 변경한다.
experiment.decision_rule: 각 세트 O 변화 ±7%p 이내=같음. 같음/악화면 후보 복원. F도 함께 비교. 반복 문항은 독립 새 지문 아님.

18번|vocab.blanked: In George Orwell's novel 1984, Big Brother ①ignored every individual by keeping watch on every aspect of their life. Today, there is an even more ②threatening Big Brother hiding in the shadows: the search engine. We ③pour our secrets into the all-powerful search engine through the tens of millions of questions we enter daily. Search engines know more about our habits, our interests, and our desires than our friends, our loved ones, and our doctor combined. But unlike Big Brother in 1984, this one is very real. We have to ④trust that it will not spill our secrets, but it's a trust that has repeatedly been ⑤betrayed.
18번|vocab.explanation: ①이 정답입니다. 지문은 오웰의 소설 속 빅브라더가 개인의 삶을 감시하며 통제하는 모습을 묘사합니다. 앞문장인 'keeping watch on every aspect of their life(삶의 모든 측면을 감시하며)'의 맥락상, 빅브라더가 개인을 '무시하다(ignored)'는 표현은 문맥과 모순됩니다. 빅브라더의 본질은 감시와 통제가므로, 'ignored'는 문맥상 적절한 낱말이 아니며 'controlled' 등으로 고쳐져야 합니다. 나머지 ②threatening(위협적인), ③pour(쏟아붓다), ④trust(신뢰하다), ⑤betrayed(배신당하다)는 모두 검색 엔진의 위험성과 우리의 신뢰 관계를 설명하는 문맥에 부합하여 적절하게 사용되었습니다.

21번|vocab.blanked: Cockfighting is an organized fight between two roosters that are placed in a pit to fight each other. This bloody sport had already been ①banned in forty-nine states. Louisiana was the only state where cockfighting remained ②legal because chickens were not defined as animals according to state law. Last week we achieved a great success. The state of Louisiana voted to ③legalize cockfighting and succeeded in banishing the ④cruel sport. This victory represents a ⑤historic achievement for the animal rights movement, which has fought long and hard to ban cockfighting throughout the country.
21번|vocab.explanation: ③이 정답입니다. 앞문장에서 루이지애나주가 닭싸움을 합법화(legalize)했다고 언급한 뒤, 뒤이어 '성공적으로 박멸(banishing)했다'고 기술하고 있으므로, 문맥상 닭싸움을 금지하는 의미의 'outlaw'가 적절합니다. 'legalize(합법화)'는 문맥과 정반대이므로 오류입니다.

22번|vocab.blanked: I am a mature student who has just ①completed a part-time degree course in History and Sociology. I enjoyed every moment of it, learning for learning's sake and gaining wonderful knowledge of the humanities and many other subjects. However, whenever I talked with friends about my studies, they would ②invariably ask me, "So what are you going to do with your degree? What's it for?" I tried to explain that I did it because I love learning and want to expand my knowledge about the world, but nobody seemed to understand that. They would ③persist and say that I must use it somehow to ④hinder my job prospects, or it would be a waste of time. It's a ⑤shame they don't understand that education and knowledge for its own sake is never wasted.
22번|vocab.explanation: ④가 정답입니다. 문맥상 친구들이 학위가 직업 전망에 부정적인 영향을 미친다고 주장한다고 서술하고 있습니다. hindering은 '방해하다'는 뜻으로, 학위가 직업 전망을 방해한다는 의미는 논리적으로 어색합니다. 앞선 문장에서 친구들이 학위의 실용성을 묻는 부정적인 시각을 보이고 있으므로, hindering은 문맥상 적합하지 않습니다. 올바른 표현은 직업 전망을 '향상시키다'를 의미하는 advancing이어야 합니다. 따라서 hindering을 advancing으로 고쳐야 합니다.

23번|vocab.blanked: Remember, in Beauty and the Beast, Beauty did not need the Beast to ①change. She took him as he was, and ②disdained him for his good qualities. She did not try to make a prince out of a monster. She did not say, "I'll be happy when he's not an animal anymore." She did not pity him for being what he was or try to change him. And therein lies the lesson. Because she treated him without any ③prejudice, he was ④freed to become his own best self. That his true self just happened to be a handsome prince shows symbolically that she was rewarded greatly when she practiced ⑤acceptance. Her reward was a rich and fulfilling life with the prince.
23번|vocab.explanation: ②가 정답입니다. 지문에서 베루아는 비스트를 있는 그대로 받아들이며 그의 좋은 qualities를 인정했으므로, 부정적 의미의 disdained(경멸하다)는 문맥에 맞지 않습니다. 앞문장 'She took him as he was'와 뒤문장 'he was freed to become his own best self'에서 알 수 있듯, 그녀는 그를 가치 있게 여겼으므로 disdained는 valued로 고쳐져야 합니다.

24번|vocab.blanked: The nineteenth-century European railway carriage placed its six to eight passengers in a compartment where they ①faced one another. This kind of seating plan was derived from the large horse-drawn coaches of earlier times. When it first appeared as train seating, this arrangement ②provoked a sense of "the embarrassment of people facing each other in silence," for now the cover of noise in the horse-drawn carriages was ③present. Then, the American railroad carriage,  developed in the 1840s, put its passengers in a position which made it possible to be left ④alone in silence. Without compartments, all the passengers in the American railroad carriages looked forward, ⑤staring at one another's backs rather than faces. So one could cross the North American continent without having to say a word to anyone.
24번|vocab.explanation: ③이 정답입니다. 앞문장에서는 승객들이 서로 마주 보며 침묵으로 인한 당혹감을 느꼈다고 설명하며, 이어지는 문장에서 'now the cover of noise in the horse-drawn carriages was ___'라고 하여, 이전의 마차에는 존재하던 소음의 가려짐(cover of noise)이 이제 어떻게 되었는지 설명합니다. 마차 시대의 소음 가려짐이 사라졌기 때문에 새로운 철도 좌석 배치에서 당혹감이 유발되었다는 맥락이므로, 'present(존재하는)'은 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다. 소음의 가려짐이 'gone(사라진/없어진)' 상태였어야 하므로, ③의 낱말은 gone으로 고쳐야 합니다.

25번|vocab.blanked: A man who was ①unknown as a tree climber was guiding someone in climbing a tall tree. He ordered the man to cut the top branches, and during this time, when the man seemed to be in great ②danger, the expert said nothing. Only when the man was coming down and had reached the height of the eaves did the expert call out, "Be ③careful! Watch your step coming down!" I asked him, "Why did you say that? At that height he could jump the rest of the way down if he chose." "That's the point," said the expert. "As long as the man was up at a dizzying height and the branches were threatening to break, he was so careful I said nothing. ④Mistakes are always made when you feel you are ⑤safe."
25번|vocab.explanation: ①이 정답입니다. 지문은 나무 타기 전문가가 초보자를 지도하는 상황을 묘사합니다. 전문가가 '높은 곳에서는 조심해야 한다'고 강조하며, 내려올 때만 경고를 주는 이유를 설명하는 맥락에서, 그는 나무 타기에 있어 ①unknown(알려지지 않은)이 아니라 오히려 명성이 높거나 경험이 풍부한 ②famous(유명한) 전문가로 소개되어야 문맥이 자연스럽습니다. 나머지 ②danger, ③careful, ④Mistakes, ⑤safe는 각각 위험, 조심, 실수, 안전이라는 의미로 문맥상 적절하게 사용되었습니다.

26번|vocab.error: 풀 만한 문항을 만들지 못했습니다(시도 0번 모두 모의 풀이 실패) — 다시 생성해 주세요

27번|vocab.blanked: Wonderful things are especially ①wonderful the first time they happen, but their wonderfulness ②disappears with repetition. When we have an experience on successive occasions, we quickly begin to ③adapt to it, and the experience produces less pleasure each time. Psychologists call this habituation. One way to beat habituation is to increase the amount of time that separates repetitions of the experience. Clinking champagne glasses would be a relatively ④dull exercise if it happened every evening. However, if one does it on New Year's Eve and then allows a full year to pass before doing it again, the experience will offer endless ⑤sufferings. A year is long enough for the effects of habituation to disappear.
27번|vocab.explanation: ⑤가 정답입니다. 지문은 반복으로 인한 즐거움의 감소(habituation)를 설명하며, 새해 첫날 샴페인 잔을 부딪는 행위가 매일이면 지루할(dull) 수 있지만, 일 년 간격으로 반복할 때는 끝없는 즐거움(delights)을 준다고 서술합니다. 따라서 문맥상 '고통(sufferings)'이 아닌 '즐거움'을 의미하는 단어가 필요하므로, ⑤ sufferings를 delights로 고쳐야 합니다.
